decisions.reason: Its dedicated product page in both 2018 and 2019 suggests performance at least near aspiration, and as a core drainage component it fits the firm's established product family and can be supported with existing slack.

The move from a mere mention in 2018 to its own page in 2019 indicates improving acceptance relative to aspiration, and floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's stated strategic direction.

Although its website prominence softened from its own page to a mention, management is likely to retain this flagship design-oriented line because of its strategic importance, learning value, and close fit with the firm's future direction.

This product had only modest visibility, so results may be more uncertain, but its contribution to installation ease and integrated shower solutions makes it a plausible line to carry while performance is still being assessed.

Being highlighted first on its own page and then on the home page is a strong signal of satisfactory results versus aspiration, so there is little behavioral reason to reallocate resources away from it.

Its lower and unchanged visibility suggests weaker evidence of success, but as a complementary drainage-related line with limited resource demands, the firm likely keeps it unless sharper performance shortfalls emerge.
